The short facts for disposal of the Rule are that on 16.10.1991 the present opposite parties No.1-3 as pre-emptors filed an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act alleging, inter-that the land measuring 6.98 acres of C.S Khatian No.12, the land measuring 12.87 acres of C.S Khatian No.90 was recorded in S.A. Khatian No.26, the land measuring 5.11 acres of C.S Khatian No.22 was recorded in S.A. Khatian No.50. The suit. land comprise .92 acres of those two S.A. Khatian. 

 9. Mr. Muhammad Rezaul Kabir Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the deed was an unregistered Ekrarnaama for security of loan money within 3 months so the application for pre-emption is not maintainable. He next submits that the vendor have no knowledge of the application for pre-emption before registration of the deed. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the lower Appellate Court as a final court of fact ought to have considered the evidence of P. W. 1 properly and due to non consideration of the evidence of P. W. 1 the lower Appellate Court has committed a serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in non-considering the oral evidence of P. W. 1 at the time of disposal of the appeal, who categorically stated that at present the suit property is not in possession of the opposite party Nos. 1 & 2 because they reconvened the land in favour of the vendor. They simply barga cultivate the land and give the lion's share of the usufructs and the defendant Nos. 3-6. The defendant Nos. I & 2 never possessed the land. From the aforesaid statements of P.W. 1 it is crystal clear that the case property was never handed over to the pre-empted opposite parties No. l & 2 the present petitioner had or has possession in the case property, the petitioners registered Kabala only for security of the loan money, the learned trial court rightly dismissed the suit which the learned Appellate Court erred in law in reversing the Judgment of the trial court and thus committed serious error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of Justice. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the vendor have no personal knowledge of the application for pre-emption before the registration of the vendor deed. He further submits that the lower appellate court as a final court of fact erred in law in not taken into consideration the depositions of P.W.1 in its true perspective and thus arrived at an erroneous finding in reversing the well reasoned judgment of the Court of I s' instance and thus the impugned judgment and order of the lower Appellate Court suffers from serious miscarriage of Justice. The learned lower Appellate Court is totally misconstrued, misconceived and thus erroneously misdirected itself in reversing the well-reasoned Judgment and order of the trial court as a result of which the impugned Judgment and order of the lower appellate Court deserves interference under the revisional jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.
